question: How many pedestrians were killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes each year from 2013 to 2025?

options.reason: Bars make the exact annual totals easy to compare across years.
options.interpretation: This bar chart answers how many pedestrians were killed in each requested year by summing the crash-level pedestrian-fatality counts; it shows annual totals from 2013 through 2025. It is a defensible framing because the requested quantity is a yearly count, and the plotted values are the direct annual sums. It does not show where or why those deaths occurred. It excludes 100545 rows dated before 2013 (4.43% of all file rows, all in the partial 2012 coverage), 36424 rows dated in 2026 (1.61% of all file rows, 2026 is covered only through 2026-06-11), and no rows for NULL crash dates or NULL pedestrian-fatality counts.

options.reason: A line emphasizes the year-to-year pattern across this ordered time series.
options.interpretation: This line chart answers how many pedestrians were killed in each requested year by summing the crash-level pedestrian-fatality counts; it shows annual totals from 2013 through 2025. It is a defensible framing because the requested quantity is a yearly count, and the plotted values are the direct annual sums. It does not show where or why those deaths occurred. It excludes 100545 rows dated before 2013 (4.43% of all file rows, all in the partial 2012 coverage), 36424 rows dated in 2026 (1.61% of all file rows, 2026 is covered only through 2026-06-11), and no rows for NULL crash dates or NULL pedestrian-fatality counts.

answer:
The bar chart shows annual pedestrian deaths of 176 in 2013; 133 in 2014; 133 in 2015; 149 in 2016; 127 in 2017; 123 in 2018; 131 in 2019; 101 in 2020; 132 in 2021; 135 in 2022; 107 in 2023; 124 in 2024; and 119 in 2025.
The line chart shows the same yearly counts—176 in 2013; 133 in 2014; 133 in 2015; 149 in 2016; 127 in 2017; 123 in 2018; 131 in 2019; 101 in 2020; 132 in 2021; 135 in 2022; 107 in 2023; 124 in 2024; and 119 in 2025—with the highest count in 2013 and lowest in 2020.
